findings.title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in UI
findings.body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only calls `onSuccess?.()` on success, whereas the sibling `disconnectMutation` explicitly invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `utils.viewer.apps.integrations` in its `onSettled`. After successfully deleting the calendar cache, the `cacheUpdatedAt`/`hasCache` state shown in the dropdown (and the 'Delete cached data' menu item) will not refresh unless the parent's `onChanged` callback happens to invalidate the same queries. This can leave the UI showing a stale 'Last updated' timestamp and a cache-deletion option that no longer corresponds to actual cache state.

findings.title: deleteCacheHandler throws a plain Error instead of TRPCError, losing proper error codes
findings.body: When the credential isn't found or doesn't belong to the user, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC will wrap this as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than a meaningful NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN code, which both misrepresents the failure to clients and can be confusing when monitoring/alerting on 500s for what is really an authorization/validation failure. It should use `TRPCError` with an appropriate code (e.g. `NOT_FOUND` or `FORBIDDEN`).

findings.title: Cache deletion authorization only checks direct credential ownership, not delegation/team-based credentials
findings.body: The handler verifies access via `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`. This does not account for delegation credentials or team-managed credentials that this codebase otherwise supports (e.g. via `enrichUserWithDelegationCredentialsIncludeServiceAccountKey`). For users accessing a Google Calendar through a delegation/organization-managed credential, this check will always fail, making the 'Delete cached data' action non-functional for those connections even though the UI may present it as available (see CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx `hasCache`, which does not exclude delegation credentials).

findings.title: hasCache does not exclude delegation credentials, so a non-functional 'Delete cached data' action can be shown
findings.body: `hasCache` is computed as `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt` without checking `delegationCredentialId`. For delegation-based Google Calendar connections that have cache entries, the dropdown will render the 'Delete cached data' menu item and allow the user to attempt deletion, but the backend `deleteCacheHandler` (which keys off `credential.userId === user.id`) will reject it for delegation credentials, resulting in a confusing failure for an action the UI implied was valid.

findings.title: Unconditional extra DB write on every cache refresh with no consumer of the updated field
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now unconditionally calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` after every cache refresh loop, updating `updatedAt` for all SelectedCalendar rows under the credential (across all event types). The PR's own notes acknowledge this value is 'currently only updated in backend... but not displayed in frontend' and question whether it should be removed. As written, this adds an unconditional, potentially frequent extra UPDATE statement (fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache can run per watched-calendar-batch/webhook) with no current UI consumer, adding unnecessary DB load/lock contention without a corresponding feature use.

findings.title: Regression: broken/errored calendar connections can no longer be disconnected when disableConnectionModification is true
findings.body: In the previous code, the Alert (error-state) branch rendered `DisconnectIntegration` guarded only by `!connectedCalendar.delegationCredentialId`, ignoring `disableConnectionModification`. The new code passes `disableConnectionModification` into `CredentialActionsDropdown`, whose internal `canDisconnect` check now also requires `!disableConnectionModification`. This means a user who previously could remove a broken/errored calendar connection even in a 'modification disabled' context (e.g. event-type scoped view) can no longer do so, which could trap users with unrecoverable broken calendar integrations in that scope.

findings.title: No tests added for new deleteCache handler, getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, or CredentialActionsDropdown component
findings.body: This PR introduces new backend logic (deleteCacheHandler, CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, enrichment of connectedCalendars with cacheUpdatedAt) and a new UI component (CredentialActionsDropdown) with non-trivial conditional rendering and multiple confirmation flows, but no unit/integration tests are included for any of them. Given these touch authorization logic (deleteCache ownership check) and data correctness (cache status mapping), lack of tests increases the risk of undetected regressions.
